title: Vulnbook
description: VulnBook is a social networking application intentionally designed with security vulnerabilities for educational and testing purposes. It includes features like user registration, posts, comments, friend requests, marketplace, and more.
long_description:
VulnBook is an intentionally vulnerable social networking application designed specifically for security education, penetration testing practice, and vulnerability research. It closely resembles a real-world social media platform, providing users with familiar functionality such as account registration and login, profile customization with bios and profile images, post creation with media attachments and hashtags, nested comment threads, likes, friend requests, real-time notifications, and search capabilities. By offering realistic features and workflows, VulnBook creates an authentic environment where security practitioners can explore how vulnerabilities emerge in modern web applications.

Beyond core social interactions, VulnBook also includes a marketplace and e-commerce system to demonstrate common business logic and financial security issues. Users can list items for sale, manage shopping carts, apply discount coupons, and complete purchases using an internal virtual currency known as VulnCash. Marketplace items require administrative approval before becoming publicly visible, simulating moderation workflows found in real platforms. These features introduce additional attack surfaces related to payment processing, coupon handling, authorization checks, and transaction validation.

The platform includes a dedicated admin panel that allows administrators to manage users, moderate reported content, approve or reject marketplace listings, and create or manage coupon codes. While these features are typical of production systems, VulnBook intentionally implements them with weak access controls and insufficient validation. This enables learners to practice exploiting authorization flaws, privilege escalation scenarios, and insecure administrative functionality, all within a controlled and ethical testing environment.

VulnBook is intentionally packed with a wide range of security vulnerabilities commonly encountered in real applications. These include plain-text password storage, SQL injection in the login system, cross-site scripting (XSS) in user-generated content, insecure direct object references (IDOR), open redirect vulnerabilities, missing CSRF protection, lack of input validation, and absence of rate limiting. In addition, the application demonstrates serious business logic flaws such as unlimited coupon reuse, missing expiration checks, virtual balance manipulation, checkout bypasses, and unsafe file upload handling. These weaknesses are deliberately left exploitable to encourage hands-on testing, manual exploitation, and vulnerability chaining.

This project is strictly intended for educational and ethical purposes and must never be deployed in a production environment. VulnBook is ideal for cybersecurity students, penetration testers, CTF players, and bug bounty hunters who want to sharpen their skills in a realistic but safe setting. By combining social networking features, e-commerce functionality, and administrative systems with intentional security flaws, VulnBook serves as a comprehensive learning platform for understanding how modern web applications fail and how attackers exploit those failures in practice.
authors: Arittro Sarkar, Shahariar Amin, Jubyer Ahmed Shezan

title: Network P-Scanner — Intelligent Network Traffic Analysis
description: Network P-scanner is a lightweight toolkit for capturing, analyzing, and visualizing network traffic (PCAP) with a small web UI and command-line helpers. It bundles scripts to capture IP traffic, build PCAPs, upload and analyze captures with tshark, and a simple web interface for review and visualization.
long_description:
Network P-Scanner is a lightweight yet powerful network traffic analysis toolkit designed to capture, inspect, and visualize PCAP data through both a web interface and command-line utilities. The project bridges low-level packet capture with higher-level security insights, making network monitoring and traffic investigation more accessible and efficient.

At its core, Network P-Scanner enables controlled packet capture from network interfaces, builds structured PCAP files, and analyzes them using tshark-based automation. The system extracts meaningful metadata, applies security heuristics, and presents results through a simple Flask-based web UI for quick review and visualization.

The toolkit is built with security research and learning in mind. It includes automated checks to detect suspicious traffic patterns, summarize network behavior, and assist in understanding how real-world traffic flows across a system. With Docker support, the entire stack can be deployed quickly in a reproducible environment.

Network P-Scanner is ideal for network analysis, cybersecurity experimentation, PCAP inspection, and educational use, offering a practical way to explore packet-level data without relying solely on heavy GUI tools.

title: Traffic-Sentinel: Log-Based Web Traffic Security Monitoring System
description: TrafficSentinel is a lightweight, log-based web traffic detection engine designed to analyze structured access logs (JSONL) from web servers such as Nginx. It detects malicious and abusive HTTP traffic using deterministic, rule-based logic, assigns per-IP scores, and emits structured security events suitable for alerting, analysis, or downstream automation. TrafficSentinel focuses on visibility, explainability, and low resource usage, rather than opaque ML models or inline request blocking.
long_description:
I’m excited to share my academic software development project Traffic-Sentinel, a lightweight, log-based web traffic detection and security monitoring system.
Traffic-Sentinel analyzes structured web server access logs (such as Nginx JSON logs) to detect malicious HTTP/HTTPS activity including SQL Injection, XSS, SSRF, brute-force attacks, scanning attempts, and automated abuse — all without inline traffic blocking or packet inspection.
The system is built around a deterministic, rule-based detection engine that emphasizes explainability, transparency, and low resource usage. Each detection is traceable to a specific rule match, and repeated malicious behavior is tracked using a per-IP reputation scoring mechanism.

Key features include:
• Real-time log-based attack detection
• Explainable rule-based analysis
• IP reputation scoring with threshold-based actions
• Brute-force attack identification
• Structured security event logging
• Optional real-time Telegram alerts
• Integration-ready outputs for tools like Fail2Ban or SIEM systems
This project was developed as part of CSE 3200 – Software Development Project II at Rajshahi University of Engineering & Technology (RUET).

The project was completed under the supervision of
Dr. Md. Shahid Uz Zaman
Professor & Head, Department of CSE, RUET

check here: https://github.com/Arittroskr32/Traffic-Sentinel

I would appreciate any feedback or suggestions from those interested in web security, log analysis, and backend system design.

title: ReconHive
description: ReconHive is a modular reconnaissance automation framework that organizes bug bounty workflows into resumable stages, automates domain-to-asset discovery, and structures attack surface intelligence into workspace-based results with built-in scope safety and tool orchestration.
long_description:
### Key Features

**Workspace-Based Recon**

Every reconnaissance run is created inside a dedicated workspace directory. This keeps all outputs, logs, and stage results organized and easy to review.

**Resumable Recon Pipeline**

ReconHive tracks execution state using a stage-based model. If a scan is interrupted, the pipeline can resume from the last completed stage without re-running previous steps.

**Stage-Oriented Recon Workflow**

ReconHive structures reconnaissance into a deterministic pipeline:

1. Subdomain Enumeration
2. Subdomain Permutation
3. DNS Resolution
4. Live Host Detection
5. Port Scanning
6. Technology Fingerprinting
7. Web Crawling
8. JavaScript Analysis
9. Parameter & Content Discovery
10. Visual Recon
11. Vulnerability Scanning

This approach allows security researchers to run recon incrementally and analyze results at each stage.

**Automated Tool Orchestration**

ReconHive integrates with commonly used reconnaissance tools such as:

- subfinder
- assetfinder
- findomain
- amass
- dnsx
- httpx
- naabu
- nmap
- nuclei

The framework handles tool execution, output management, and result consolidation automatically.

**Scope-Aware Reconnaissance**

ReconHive enforces strict scope rules by parsing in-scope and out-of-scope definitions. All discovered assets are filtered against scope rules before active scanning stages are executed, helping prevent accidental out-of-scope activity.

**Structured Recon Data**

Results are stored in organized directories that separate data by recon stage, making it easier to analyze attack surfaces and track findings across large engagements.

---

### Why I Built ReconHive

Bug bounty reconnaissance often involves chaining multiple tools together while manually managing outputs and scope rules. This process quickly becomes messy, error-prone, and difficult to resume.

ReconHive was built to solve this problem by providing:

- A structured reconnaissance pipeline
- Safe scope-aware scanning workflows
- Organized artifact storage
- Resumable stage execution

The goal is to make reconnaissance **repeatable, scalable, and easier to manage during large attack surface assessments.**

---

## Example Workflow

### Initialize a workspace

```bash
python reconhive init -i in-scope.txt -o out-of-scope.txt -w recon_runs/target
```

### Run recon stages

```bash
python reconhive run --stage enum -w recon_runs/target
python reconhive run --stage resolve -w recon_runs/target
python reconhive run --stage live -w recon_runs/target
```

### Check execution progress
```bash
python reconhive status -w recon_runs/target
```

---

## Project Goals

- Automate repetitive reconnaissance tasks
- Maintain strict scope safety for bug bounty programs
- Provide structured and resumable recon workflows
- Simplify attack surface mapping for large targets
technologies: Python, nmap, Nuclei, httpx, dnsx, subfinder

title: VulnAtlas — Self-Hosted Bug Bounty Knowledge Base
description: VulnAtlas — A self-hosted bug bounty research dashboard to organize vulnerability methodology, checklists, resources, and reference files with full-text search and role-based access control.
long_description:
VulnAtlas is a full-stack web application I designed and built to solve a real problem I faced as a bug bounty hunter — the lack of a centralized, private, and structured place to store all my security research. Instead of scattered notes, random bookmarks, and loose files across different tools, VulnAtlas brings everything into one clean, self-hosted dashboard accessible from any browser.

At its core, the application is a vulnerability knowledge base where I can document detailed entries for each vulnerability type — including testing methodology, indicators of compromise, common mistakes, evidence notes, and reporting tips. Alongside this, a functionality checklist module lets me map application features to relevant vulnerability types, ensuring thorough and consistent test coverage across every engagement.

The platform also includes a resource manager for organizing curated reference links with tags and technology labels, a file manager for uploading and categorizing research files like PDFs, writeups, and proof-of-concept screenshots, and a powerful Hunt Explorer that supports full-text and multi-filter search across all vulnerability entries by keyword, category, technology, tag, status code, and request type.

Security and access control were taken seriously from the start. The app uses role-based authentication — a single admin account with full create, read, update, and delete access, alongside unlimited read-only viewer accounts for sharing research with teammates. An admin panel allows password management and user administration without touching any configuration files.

On the technical side, VulnAtlas is built with Python 3.12 and Flask, uses SQLite as a zero-configuration file-based database, and is fully containerized with Docker and Docker Compose for a one-command deployment. The frontend uses Tailwind CSS for a clean, responsive UI, and Gunicorn serves the application in production. All data — the database and uploaded files — persists in a named Docker volume, surviving container restarts and rebuilds.
technologies: Python, Flask, SQLite, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, Docker
